title: Investing STILL Won't Make You Rich (Probably)
summary: Investing is a tool, not a shortcut: after tax and inflation market returns take decades to build wealth; sellers of life-changing returns are transferring the risk to buyers.

assertions.quote: investing or even speculating won't make you rich in the short term probably

verdicts.note: At real after-tax returns near five percent, modest savings take decades to reach seven figures.

assertions.quote: the return that you actually see is closer to 5.4 4% almost half of the original return

verdicts.note: Taxes and roughly three percent inflation cut a ten percent nominal return to about half in real after-tax terms.

assertions.quote: Warren Buffett are on record for only earning a only a long-term average return of 20 to 30%
these returns were all temporary they were all short-term returns that moderated over the long term

verdicts.note: Bubble-era asset returns reverted after the dot-com and crypto cycles.

assertions.quote: most people aren't even able to achieve the market return Thanks to behavioral biases
the asset class that you put your money into tends to play a bigger role in the return you see than security selection

verdicts.note: Brinson-style attribution studies find allocation explains most return variation across portfolios.

assertions.quote: the vast majority of clients have gone to that point by either owning a business having a very high paying job

verdicts.note: Wealth surveys show business ownership, high earnings, saving and inheritance dominate millionaire origins.

assertions.quote: most of the time they didn't make their own money from that thing but rather either the selling of that program
why to you and not a hedge fund that could pay millions if not billions Upfront for a proven investing strategy
